item.title: [53★] Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
item.author: Sergey Shirobokov, ..., Michael Broughton, et al (5)
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 53 ★

Authors: Sergey Shirobokov, ..., Michael Broughton, et al (5)

arXiv ID: 2611.09822 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

Sergey Shirobokov, ..., Michael Broughton, et al (5)

item.title: [43★] A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
item.author: David Turturean
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 43 ★

Authors: David Turturean

arXiv ID: 2611.09773 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that every bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. They showed that the conjecture implies that the acceptance probability of every quantum algorithm making TT queries can be approximated on most inputs by a classical algorithm making poly(T)\mathrm{poly}(T) queries. We prove their conjecture: every function f:{−1,1}n→[−1,1]f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1] of degree at most d≥1d\ge1 has a variable of influence at least cVar(f)5/2/d6c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^{6}, where c>0c>0 is an absolute constant. In the original formulation, for polynomials of degree at most dd with values in [0,1][0,1] on {0,1}n\{0,1\}^n and variance at least ε\varepsilon, this gives a variable of influence at least (ε/d)7(\varepsilon/d)^{7}. The proof is elementary, with steps inspired by works of others. Thus, as Aaronson and Ambainis anticipated, superpolynomial quantum speedups in the query model require structure, such as a promise on the inputs.

David Turturean

item.title: [26★] What are local complementations, really?
item.author: Kenneth Goodenough
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 26 ★

Authors: Kenneth Goodenough

arXiv ID: 2611.08620 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A local complementation at a vertex vv of a graph GG replaces the induced neighborhood of vv with its complement. Local complementations are, at face value, peculiar operations. Yet they famously show up when describing the local Clifford equivalence among graph states, and, because of this, have become a fundamental notion in the study of graph states. Following Bouchet, we show here how local complementations on graphs are more naturally thought of in terms of switchings of (matroid) bases of stabilizer states. Bases and switchings reveal structural properties of stabilizer states that are harder to glean from the graph-theoretic description alone, such as vertex-minors and statistics of local Pauli measurements. Bases also simplify prior proofs about graphs up to local complementations, of which we give several examples. Bases are foundational in the study of (multi)matroids; as such this paper serves as a gentle introduction to the applications of multimatroids to quantum information theory.

Kenneth Goodenough

item.title: [16★] Magic Can Superactivate Quantum Capacity
item.author: Chunhe Xiong, ..., Shao-Ming Fei, Junde Wu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Chunhe Xiong, ..., Shao-Ming Fei, Junde Wu

arXiv ID: 2611.09594 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Environmental magic can enable two channels with zero quantum capacity to transmit quantum information jointly. We establish this superactivation within a family of discrete quantum convolution channels with fixed Clifford interactions. For the couplings considered, stabilizer-mixture environments induce entanglement-breaking channels. We construct a mixed magic environment whose induced channel has positive private capacity and a Choi state with positive partial transpose, hence zero quantum capacity. A half-erasure auxiliary activates this channel through the Smith--Yard mechanism. Finite-block encoding and decoding over a self-complementary convolution auxiliary then realize a higher-dimensional erasure channel that still permits activation. We also bound the activated capacity by the modified relative entropy of magic of the main environment. Replacing either environment of the convolution pair by any stabilizer mixture makes the joint quantum capacity vanish, identifying environmental magic as a necessary resource on both sides for this realization.

Chunhe Xiong, ..., Shao-Ming Fei, Junde Wu

item.title: [16★] Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
item.author: Tatsuya Yamanouchi, Naoto Shiraishi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 16 ★

Authors: Tatsuya Yamanouchi, Naoto Shiraishi

arXiv ID: 2611.08974 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.

Tatsuya Yamanouchi, Naoto Shiraishi

item.title: [14★] Optimal Separations Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity under Permutation Symmetry
item.author: Yunqi Huang, ..., Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 14 ★

Authors: Yunqi Huang, ..., Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng

arXiv ID: 2611.08919 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

A function f:\cD⊆AN→{0,1}f:\cD\subseteq A^N\to\{0,1\} is \emphpermutation-invariant if every permutation of its input positions preserves both its domain and its value. We study how this symmetry limits quantum speedups. For 1/6≤ε<1/21/6\leq\varepsilon<1/2, we prove that every such function over an arbitrary finite alphabet AA satisfies Rε(f)=O(Qε(f)2)R_\varepsilon(f)=O(Q_\varepsilon(f)^2), where RεR_\varepsilon and QεQ_\varepsilon denote randomized and quantum query complexities with error at most ε\varepsilon. This improves the previous cubic bound (ITCS 2019). We further establish bounds for graph and hypergraph properties, for which vertex relabeling preserves both the promise and the answer. For the same range of ε\varepsilon, we obtain Rε(f)=O(Qε(f)4)R_\varepsilon(f)=O(Q_\varepsilon(f)^4) for graph properties in the adjacency-matrix model and Rε(f)=Ok(Qε(f)2k)R_\varepsilon(f)=O_k(Q_\varepsilon(f)^{2k}) for kk-uniform hypergraph properties with fixed k≥2k\geq2, where the implicit constant depends only on kk. These improve the previous bounds R1/3(f)=O(Q1/3(f)6)R_{1/3}(f)=O(Q_{1/3}(f)^6) and R1/3(f)=Ok(Q1/3(f)3k)R_{1/3}(f)=O_k(Q_{1/3}(f)^{3k}), respectively (SICOMP 2024) These bounds are tight for permutation-invariant functions and nearly tight for graph and hypergraph properties. Unstructured search gives a matching quadratic separation with R1/3(f)=Θ(Q1/3(f)2)R_{1/3}(f)=\Theta\!\left(Q_{1/3}(f)^2\right). For every fixed k≥2k\geq 2, we construct explicit families of invariant promise problems on kk-uniform hypergraphs satisfying R1/3(f)≥Q1/3(f)2k−o(1)R_{1/3}(f)\geq Q_{1/3}(f)^{2k-o(1)}.

item.title: [13★] Shared Lookups and Lazy Residues: Fewer Toffoli Gates for Factoring RSA-2048
item.author: Monit Sharma, Hoong Chuin Lau
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 13 ★

Authors: Monit Sharma, Hoong Chuin Lau

arXiv ID: 2611.08907 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gidney's 2025 construction for factoring RSA-2048 with few logical qubits spends most of its Toffoli gates on discrete-log table lookups and residue uncomputation. We reduce both costs. Shared lookups return entries for several primes of a residue number system at once because they have the same address. Retained intermediate residues remove recomputation during cleanup and enable lazy arithmetic with a single final modular reduction. We prove output preservation and estimate resources with an open benchmark built on the reference simulator. Against the best reference setting within the same logical-qubit budget, using the published model for the reference and benchmark counts for our circuits, we obtain 15%15\% fewer Toffolis at 1,4611{,}461 qubits (5.08×1095.08 \times 10^{9} per factoring) and 46%46\% fewer at 1,8061{,}806 qubits (2.55×1092.55 \times 10^{9}). A matched ablation finds 28.8%28.8\% fewer Toffolis from three-prime sharing at fixed window and checkpoint settings. Architecture-specific timing determines how much becomes a runtime saving.

Monit Sharma, Hoong Chuin Lau

item.title: [13★] Exploring topological signatures of quantum Fisher information scaling in graph states
item.author: Majid Hassani, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 13 ★

Authors: Majid Hassani, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura

arXiv ID: 2611.08593 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Graph states are a versatile resource for quantum metrology, and their quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a closed-form expression in terms of the underlying graph: it counts pairs of vertices with identical neighborhoods. It remains unclear, however, which global structural properties of a graph determine whether its QFI exceeds the standard quantum limit (SQL). Here we ask whether topological invariants, namely the Betti numbers of the graph's clique complex, capture this behavior, and we address the question numerically with two complementary approaches. First, we randomly add or delete edges in balanced complete multipartite graphs, which combine a QFI beyond the SQL with a single nonvanishing higher Betti number. Edge addition eventually destroys both the metrological advantage and the nontrivial topology. Under edge deletion, by contrast, higher Betti numbers persist well after the QFI has dropped to the SQL. Second, we start from Erdős--Rényi random graphs, whose QFI does not typically exceed the SQL, and maximize a chosen Betti number with a Monte Carlo search. The search drives the graphs toward near-extremal multipartite structures whose QFI lies well beyond the SQL. Our results show that topological optimization offers a route to metrologically useful graph states, but also that Betti numbers alone do not determine the QFI.

Majid Hassani, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura

item.title: [12★] Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
item.author: Llorenç Escolà-Farràs, Florian Speelman
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 12 ★

Authors: Llorenç Escolà-Farràs, Florian Speelman

arXiv ID: 2611.09504 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement (MoE) game has numerous applications in quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, position verification, and unclonable encryption. In this short note, we improve the error threshold for parallel repetition with identical answer strings from the approximately 3.7%3.7\% certified by the original bound to the sharp threshold (1−1/√2)/2≈14.64%(1-1/\sqrt2)/2\approx14.64\%. When the players need not give identical answers, we also obtain exponential decay whenever the sum of their error tolerances is below this threshold. These bounds strengthen existing security reductions to the BB84 MoE game, improving security bounds and certified noise tolerances for cryptographic protocols.

Llorenç Escolà-Farràs, Florian Speelman

item.title: [10★] Twisted Compactification, Quotient Quantum Codes and Logical Gates
item.author: Po-Shen Hsin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 10 ★

Authors: Po-Shen Hsin

arXiv ID: 2611.09538 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Many quantum codes, including balanced-product, bivariate-bicycle and genon codes and the five-qubit code, are quotient codes: a larger code folded onto itself by identifying each check with its image under a deck transformation composed with a symmetry. We show that this is the lattice form of twisted compactification, in which a theory on X×FX\times F carries a symmetry background along FF, and we use the correspondence in both directions. For monomial quotients of Pauli stabilizer codes, a transfer theorem gives the logical qudits, logical operators and distance bounds from those of the parent, with a Tate cohomology group counting the logical operators that are new. For higher-form and cup-product symmetries the twist is an entangling diagonal circuit; when a finite cover trivializes the background, the code is a dressed quotient, so abelian Pauli codes give non-abelian topological order such as D(D4)D(D_4). The dressings have Clifford level at most one less than the degree of the twist, and for cubic twists the code dimension is a count of solutions of quadratic equations in cup products, which certifies that the code is not a Pauli stabilizer code when it is not a power of two; on tori and slabs the distance is linear in the size. Twists also create logical gates: three toric codes on S3S^3 have no logical qubits, but on RP3\mathbb{RP}^3 the same circuit is a logical CCZCCZ. A quarter-turn twist of the 3D fermionic toric code gives codes of linear distance, from [[768,2,9]][[768,2,9]] up, whose p+ipp+ip pump is an explicit finite-time quasi-local evolution that preserves the code space exactly; using the spin-topological response formula of Barkeshli, Hsin and Kobayashi, we identify its logical action as TT up to Clifford factors. Finally, twisting abelian gauge theories reach only the quantum doubles D(G)D(G) with [G,G][G,G] central.

Po-Shen Hsin

item.title: [9★] Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
item.author: Vittorio Pagni, ..., Michael Epping, Kevin Lively
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Vittorio Pagni, ..., Michael Epping, Kevin Lively

arXiv ID: 2611.09760 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Efficient encoding of data into quantum states remains a fundamental bottleneck in many quantum computing protocols, which would otherwise offer advantages over their classical counterparts. Here, we introduce deterministic and scalable amplitude-encoding methods with low two-qubit gate costs and tunable trade-offs between circuit depth and encoding fidelity. Our approaches require no amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurement and are capable of encoding arbitrary complex data or queryable functions by using tensor-networks to go beyond what can be held in classical memory. Our principle contributions are two complementary algorithms for simplifying fully controlled multiplexer circuits to one- and two-qubit gates. In the first, we formally map the elimination of redundant gate controls to a Boolean logic minimization problem, while in the second we utilize a single ancilla qubit to map the multi-controlled rotation gates to a sequence of one- and two-qubit operations via the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of the gate angles. We benchmark these methods across a broad range of function classes, characterizing their total depth in an all-to-all connectivity graph against system size and target fidelity. Hybridizing our methods gives up to orders of magnitude improvement in circuit depth at equivalent state fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in the Qiskit package. We furthermore demonstrate our method on IQM hardware with a square lattice connectivity, finding excellent fidelity, even with minimal noise mitigation. By significantly reducing gate depth for encoding, this work enables the experimental execution of applications on current and near-term hardware which would otherwise be reduced to noise before the first calculation step, shortening the time horizon to robust quantum utility.

Vittorio Pagni, ..., Michael Epping, Kevin Lively

item.title: [6★] Beyond the n/2n/2 Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
item.author: Yuan Deng, ..., Jianan Shao, David P. Woodruff
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Yuan Deng, ..., Jianan Shao, David P. Woodruff

arXiv ID: 2611.09809 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every nn-bit Boolean function with bounded error using n/2+O(√n)n/2+O(\sqrt n) quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using ⌈n/2⌉\lceil n/2\rceil queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond n/2n/2 is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring n/2+Ω(n1/3)n/2+\Omega(n^{1/3}) quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using n/2+O(n1/3)n/2+O(n^{1/3}) quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

Yuan Deng, ..., Jianan Shao, David P. Woodruff

item.title: [6★] Neutral-atom quantum features as complementary structural encodings for graph learning
item.author: Mathieu Garrigues, ..., Lorenzo Moro, Shaheen Acheche
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Mathieu Garrigues, ..., Lorenzo Moro, Shaheen Acheche

arXiv ID: 2611.08821 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Structural descriptors provide graph neural networks (GNNs) with positional and topological inductive biases. However, widely used classical encodings based on random walks or Laplacian spectra emphasize specific structural statistics of a graph, leaving room for alternative descriptors. Neutral-atom quantum processing units (QPUs) can realize graph-dependent Rydberg Hamiltonians, allowing graph topology to be probed through dynamical correlation measurements. In this work, we use these measurements as quantum graph features (QGFs), providing a complementary, hardware-derived family of structural encoding that is not accurately described by classical features derived from Laplacian and adjacency matrices, even when supplemented with an extended set of random-walk, geometric descriptors and classical physical models. By appropriately selecting the quench parameters of the Hamiltonian, we access two characteristic correlation regimes with distinct structural signatures: antiferromagnetic-like and ferromagnetic-like. On an intrinsic information benchmark of 15 topological and spectral probing tasks, quantum and hybrid quantum-classical features match or surpass classical descriptors on local topological properties. When supplied to message-passing, attention, and graph-transformer backbones, hybrid quantum-classical features yield improvements that are within cross-fold noise on most cells but sign-consistent across architectures. When comparing noiseless, shot-sampled emulation-derived quantum features with a neutral-atom QPU implementation, the downstream hybrid results with compressed hardware features match their emulated counterparts within 0.010.01 F1_1 on all backbones. On a synthetic family of ladder graphs, QGFs distinguish two specific classes, outperforming the strongest classical structural descriptors by a margin exceeding cross-fold variability.

Mathieu Garrigues, ..., Lorenzo Moro, Shaheen Acheche

item.title: [6★] Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
item.author: James W. T. Keeble, ..., Federico Rocco, Martin J. Savage
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: James W. T. Keeble, ..., Federico Rocco, Martin J. Savage

arXiv ID: 2611.08776 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, MNLαM^{\mathrm{NL}}_\alpha, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, FA{F}_A. We calculate stabilizer Rényi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound 4FA≤MNLlin4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}} holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.

James W. T. Keeble, ..., Federico Rocco, Martin J. Savage

item.title: [6★] Random encoders and expurgation improve 1,873 entries of the Grassl qubit code tables
item.author: Marin Girard
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Marin Girard

arXiv ID: 2611.08744 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

I report 192 explicit binary stabilizer codes [[n,k,d]][[n,k,d]] with 53≤n≤25453\le n\le 254 and 5≤d≤135\le d\le 13 whose minimum distance exceeds the lower bound listed in Grassl's code tables at the same (n,k)(n,k): 161 codes by one and 31 by two. Through the standard propagation rules they raise 1,873 entries of the table. For 190 of the codes, a random Clifford encoder is followed by expurgation: every logical operator of weight below the target distance is enumerated, and a few logical operators are promoted to stabilizers so that each low-weight one anticommutes with at least one of them. The other two are obtained by puncturing a code from the table and repairing it in the same way. All 192 distances are exact: the lower bound is certified by exhaustive meet-in-the-middle enumeration of up to 4×10134\times10^{13} Pauli operators, and the upper bound by an explicit logical operator of weight dd. A first-moment count explains the results. Expurgated random codes have about eight more logical qubits than a typical random code of the same length and distance, so they beat the table wherever its best known codes are no better than random. The largest gains, up to nine logical qubits, are at d≥9d\ge9 and n≳170n\gtrsim170, where the table often gives a lower bound without an explicit code. The same count predicts improvements at 619 further pairs (n,d)(n,d). The search was run by AI agents. The codes, their certificates and an independent checker are public.

Marin Girard

item.title: [5★] Tomography of approximately Gaussian mixed states
item.author: S. Nibedita Swain, ..., Jens Eisert, Nathan Walk
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: S. Nibedita Swain, ..., Jens Eisert, Nathan Walk

arXiv ID: 2611.09322 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Moment-based tomography efficiently reconstructs Gaussian states, but stochastic phase noise generally produces mixed, non-Gaussian outputs. For approximately Gaussian outputs, we formulate reconstruction as a problem in quantum learning theory under model misspecification. Our trace-distance guarantee separates the intrinsic Gaussian approximation error from statistical errors in estimating the first moments and covariance matrix. Using recent Gaussian trace-distance bounds, we obtain linear dependence of the statistical contribution on moment errors when the covariance inverses remain bounded, improving on the square-root dependence on covariance error in earlier guarantees. A Fock-space truncation procedure provides certified, convergent lower and upper bounds on the intrinsic error. Under an explicit sub-Gaussian condition on the heterodyne outcomes, the sufficient sample count scales inversely with the square of the allowed statistical error remaining after accounting for the approximation error. We verify the statistical condition for stochastic phase rotations and heralded unitary-averaged states with bounded input squeezing. We apply the framework to probabilistic unitary averaging for phase noise reduction, quantifying reconstruction error and accounting for heralding overhead in the total number of estimation attempts.

S. Nibedita Swain, ..., Jens Eisert, Nathan Walk

item.title: [5★] Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure
item.author: Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang

arXiv ID: 2611.08586 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in Møller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give sin2θW=1/4\sin^2\theta_W=1/4 at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.

Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang

item.title: [3★] Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
item.author: Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima

arXiv ID: 2611.09540 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can induce a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. Here, we answer this question systematically. We first construct an explicit model and prove that coupling to an environment can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system, even without such resource supply. We consider Lindblad master equations with (i) time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, (ii) time-translation covariance, and (iii) detailed balance---conditions that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. Our model satisfies these conditions, and the activation occurs in a stationary state of both the isolated and open systems. We give several implementations of this dynamics with a zero-temperature Gibbs environment, a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, and only short-range Hamiltonians, one of which exactly reproduces the time-crystalline periodicity. We then prove a no-go theorem: under (i)--(iii), activation can arise only from an environment-induced Hamiltonian term, not from dissipation. Our results show that time crystals can be activated in open systems without external resource supply and identify the physical requirements on the system and environment for this activation through our general no-go theorem.

Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima

item.title: [3★] Harnessing dimensional leakage for continuous-variable randomness certification
item.author: Moisés Alves, ..., Alexandre B. Tacla, Rafael Chaves
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Moisés Alves, ..., Alexandre B. Tacla, Rafael Chaves

arXiv ID: 2611.08607 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Semi-device-independent quantum protocols often rely on strict Hilbert-space dimension assumptions that are difficult to satisfy in realistic implementations, particularly with infinite-dimensional optical fields. The almost-qudit framework addresses this issue by quantifying the leakage of quantum states beyond a target subspace. Although such leakage can severely compromise randomness certification for fixed preparation and measurement inputs, we show that averaging over the full input ensemble can mitigate this vulnerability and extend the range of tolerable leakage. This enhanced robustness enables nonzero randomness certification using low-squeezing single-mode Gaussian states and homodyne detection, thus offering an experimentally accessible continuous-variable implementation.

Moisés Alves, ..., Alexandre B. Tacla, Rafael Chaves

item.title: [3★] Universality in Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
item.author: Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina

arXiv ID: 2611.08590 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.

Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina

item.title: [3★] Thermodynamics of Speed and Efficiency with Quantum Feedback
item.author: Yue Liu, ..., Ruicheng Bao, Tan Van Vu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Yue Liu, ..., Ruicheng Bao, Tan Van Vu

arXiv ID: 2611.08564 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Rapid thermodynamic operations generally entail irreversible dissipation, giving rise to trade-offs between operating speed and thermodynamic cost. Yet, how quantum feedback fundamentally reshapes these trade-offs remains elusive. Here, we derive a finite-time current--dissipation relation for continuously monitored open quantum dynamics with jump feedback. From this fundamental relation, we establish a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency trade-off for stationary information engines, identifying how feedback affects state transformations and the performance of engines through both informational entropy and direct dynamical contributions. Our results provide a quantitative foundation for fast, low-dissipation quantum thermodynamics in the presence of feedback control, exemplified by attaining the generalized Landauer bound in finite-time information erasure and approaching unit information efficiency at finite power in the large-system limit of a collective engine.

Yue Liu, ..., Ruicheng Bao, Tan Van Vu

item.title: [2★] Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
item.author: Yu-Ning Zhang, ..., David P. DiVincenzo, Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski

Abstract:

Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated 1/f1/f noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

Authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Pablo Vielman, Miguel Gonzalez

arXiv ID: 2611.09230 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

How a quantum resource can be quantified depends on which operations are free. Yet two proposed quantifiers of quantum state texture can increase under free operations: the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information relative to the unique textureless state and the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance from that state. We show reachability from every state orthogonal to the textureless state, whether pure or mixed: each can be freely transformed into any other state. Therefore, every texture monotone must assign the same maximal value to all such states, a requirement that neither candidate satisfies. We then construct valid texture monotones by adding the population outside the textureless state to the skew information and by maximizing the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance over free operations. We prove faithfulness, convexity, and invariance under textureless ancillas, characterize additivity properties and strong monotonicity, satisfied only in the Wigner-Yanase case, and derive tight bounds for both monotones at fixed overlap with the textureless state and characterize all saturating states. Together, these results show how allowed state transformations impose operational constraints on the quantification of quantum state texture.

Abstract:

We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited 1/f1/f noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.

Abstract:

Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H2_2 is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H2_2 confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H2_2 and para-H2_2 states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO2_2 and N2_2O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H2_2 concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H2_2 loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H2_2 clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H2_2 loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

Abstract:

Efficient implementation of the operations required for quantum error correction in superconducting quantum computers requires high gate fidelity, adequate qubit connectivity, and selective control of interactions. Sharing a single coupler among multiple qubits can improve connectivity, but also requires accounting for its effects on qubits outside the target pair. In this work, we numerically investigate the feasibility of implementing parametric-resonance CZ\mathrm{CZ} gates in a tunable tripod structure consisting of three fixed-frequency transmon qubits connected to a single tunable coupler. We modulate the external flux applied to the coupler and optimize the pulse parameters for each qubit pair to construct CZ01\mathrm{CZ}_{01}, CZ02\mathrm{CZ}_{02}, and CZ12\mathrm{CZ}_{12} gates. We calculate the time evolution of a Hamiltonian that includes three energy levels for each circuit element and evaluate gate fidelity and leakage after virtual Z correction. The fidelities obtained for the target-pair computational blocks, whose input and output basis states have both the coupler and spectator qubit in their ground states, are 0.9943, 0.9834, and 0.9907, respectively. We also find that population preservation at the end of the gate depends on the initial state of the spectator qubit. These results demonstrate the possibility of constructing CZ\mathrm{CZ} operations for each qubit pair through flux modulation of a shared coupler while maintaining fixed data-qubit frequencies. They also highlight the need to evaluate performance and optimize control over the full computational space, including the spectator qubit.

item.author: J. A. Crosse
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: J. A. Crosse

arXiv ID: 2611.08906 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

When deriving the expression for the Noether's current one obtains a term that is an integral over the Euler-Lagrange equation. This term vanishes along the classical path and so does not contribute to the current. However, quantum particles do not necessarily follow the classical path; this concept is the basis of Feynman's path integral quantization formalism. Thus, for a quantum system, the Euler-Lagrange term does not vanish and, hence, corresponds to a quantum fluctuation of the Noether's current owing to the system deviating from the classical path. Here, we compute this quantum fluctuation from Noether's theorem and the path integral formalism. We find that, for a time invariant system, the expression for the quantum fluctuations is give by minus the functional expression for the Hamiltonian, ΔE=−H(y)\Delta E = -H(y), evaluated at the distance from the classical path, yy. As an example we evaluate quantum energy fluctuations of a single Harmonic oscillator. In the short time limit we recover the energy-time uncertainty relation and in the long time limit we recover the zero point energy of the quantum harmonic oscillator.

Authors: Matthew Herbst, ..., Jinhoon Jeong, Mika A. Sillanpää

arXiv ID: 2611.08619 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.

Abstract:

The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

Authors: Josep Cabedo, ..., Leticia Tarruell, Alessio Celi

arXiv ID: 2611.09855 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled 39^{39}K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.

Authors: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

arXiv ID: 2611.09839 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Rényi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

item.author: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee, ..., S D Sudarsan, Gudapati Naresh Raghava

Authors: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee, ..., S D Sudarsan, Gudapati Naresh Raghava

arXiv ID: 2611.09830 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of deterministic quantum search to NP problems while retaining the quadratic query advantage over classical exhaustive search.

arXiv ID: 2611.09814 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

Abstract:

Abstract:

Abstract:

Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.
